html:
Between 1580 and 1640, while Spain and Portugal shared one king in the Iberian Union, Portuguese merchants spread through Spanish America. They opened shops and trading houses in Lima, Buenos Aires, Cartagena and Mexico City.

Their great prize was the silver of Potosí. Officially it had to go out through Lima and the Spanish fleets. Much of it was instead smuggled down to Buenos Aires and out to Brazil, Lisbon and Africa. In return the Portuguese brought enslaved Africans, since they held the contracts to supply them, and linked Spanish America to the Atlantic slave trade.

Many of these merchants were New Christians, descendants of Jews forced to convert. That made them targets. In 1639 the Inquisition in Lima burned eleven people after a trial known as the Great Complicity, most of them Portuguese merchants.

Portugal broke away from Spain in 1640, and suspicion of the Portuguese in Spanish America grew sharply.
sum: Between 1580 and 1640, while Spain and Portugal shared one king in the Iberian Union, Portuguese merchants spread through Spanish America. They opened shops and trading houses in Lima, Buenos Aires, Cartagena and Mexico City.
